patient-oriented treatment accompanying data collection and documentation is the basis to evaluate medical care in a patient's perspective.

patient-oriented, treatment accompanying documentation can serve as a basis for the evaluation of quality of medical care and that it is an essential tool for the development of clinical practice guidelines.
the patient oriented treatment accompanying documentation is an important tool for the quality management in oncology.

the development, evaluation and optimisation of a patient-oriented, treatment-accompanied documentation system in oncology.
the evaluation of quality of care in oncology and its implications towards clinical practice.

the quality of care can be improved by the systematic documentation of the clinical course of the disease, the applied interventions and the patients' outcome in the course of time.

a patient-oriented documentation of the treatment course and outcome of a patient with cancer is a valuable tool to support quality assurance, to improve the quality of care and to evaluate the effectiveness of medical interventions.
a patient-oriented treatment-accompanying data collection is an important basis for the evaluation of quality of care in medical oncology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have to find a way to combine the best of two worlds: the "real world" and the "research world".
a treatment accompanying documentation is a necessary basis for the assessment and evaluation of medical oncology in the context of clinical practice guidelines.
the documentation of the treatment of cancer patients should be a patient-oriented, treatment-accompanied and quality-oriented process.

a systematic documentation of the medical care of patients is necessary to improve quality of care.
a patient-oriented treatment documenting system has to be designed in a way that allows for an easy integration into daily clinical routine.
